records.name: Acre

A current-status check confirms the federal framework (marriage equality since 2013, no criminalisation, nationwide document rectification) unchanged. No state-level hostility mechanism is on record.

records.name: Puducherry
records.current_summary: Puducherry is a union territory with a partial legislature: recognition and welfare policy for trans people is set principally by the federal government, and no Puducherry-specific statute, enforcement series or incident pattern is on file.  The framework that governs it shifted sharply in March 2026: parliament passed an amendment removing the self-identification right affirmed by the 2014 Supreme Court ruling, restricting legal recognition to historically recognised communities (hijra/kinnar) and intersex people, mandating medical certification for identity documents and for surgery; critics and a court-appointed advisory panel warn it excludes many trans, non-binary and gender-fluid people, protests followed the vote in several cities, and the change bears uniformly on every state and territory.  Nationally recurring policing practice — treating trans appearance as a suspicion category in transit spaces, evidenced by an August 2024 railway-platform groping complaint (an FIR was filed and intrusive questioning reported) — reaches union-territory visitors through federal transport policing rather than any local law.

sources.claim: The 2026 Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill amends the 2019 law: it removes the right to self-identification, limits legal recognition to historically accepted categories and intersex individuals, and mandates medical certification for identity recognition - HRW calls it a major reversal of the 2014 rights and urges the president not to sign it (articles dated 26 Mar 2026).

Amendment bill approved by both houses (article 2026, awaiting presidential assent): removes the self-identification right affirmed by the 2014 Supreme Court 'third gender' ruling; narrows the 2019 definition of transgender person; government says the narrower definition improves welfare delivery, critics warn it excludes trans men, trans women, non-binary and gender-fluid people; mandatory medical certification described as an attack on privacy and dignity.

records.name: Sikkim
records.current_summary: No Sikkim-specific trans statute, enforcement series or incident pattern is on file; the state sits under the national framework, which narrowed sharply in March 2026: parliament removed the self-identification right affirmed by the 2014 Supreme Court ruling, restricted recognition to intersex variations and traditional community identities certified by medical boards, and made board certification mandatory for gender-affirming surgery. A court-appointed advisory panel asked the government to withdraw the bill, prominent trans activists warned of mass exclusion, protests followed the vote, and presidential assent is pending.  The framework's enforcement texture nationally includes transit-space 'gender checks': an August 2024 case at a northern railway station, in which a trans traveller alleged a rail-police constable groped her while checking her gender — police denied it and filed a counter-complaint — evidences a policing habit of treating trans appearance as suspicion in federally-policed transit spaces rather than in this state specifically.

records.name: Mizoram
records.current_summary: No Mizoram-specific trans statute or enforcement record is on file; the union of national law governs recognition here. In March 2026 that national framework narrowed significantly: both houses passed an amendment to the 2019 trans persons law removing self-identification, restricting legal recognition to biologically-verified and traditional-community categories, and mandating medical-board certification for gender-affirming surgery. The bill drew nationwide protests from the community and opposition parties, a Supreme Court-appointed advisory panel asked the government to withdraw it, and presidential assent remained pending as of late March 2026.  Neither international reporting on the change nor any other source on file records Mizoram-level deviation — statute, ban, or enforcement campaign — in either direction; the northeast state's day-to-day exposure for a trans visitor therefore runs through the central framework, its pending narrowing included.

sources.claim: HRW report (26 Mar 2026): India's parliament passed the 2026 Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill narrowing the 2019 law: it removes self-identification, restricts legal recognition to traditionally recognised groups (hijra/kinner) and intersex persons, and requires medical certification for identity recognition — reversing the 2014 Supreme Court ruling. The bill adds offences including up to life imprisonment for 'coercing or alluring' anyone to be transgender, which HRW warns could criminalise support networks. Of 487,803 census-recorded transgender persons, only about 32,500 hold identity cards. HRW urges the president not to sign; assent pending as of late March 2026.

BBC (26 Mar 2026): India's parliament passed an amendment to the 2019 transgender-rights law replacing self-identification with recognition based on biological or physical traits plus traditional identities (hijra/kinner-style); medical boards and district authorities must now certify gender-affirming surgery. The government says the narrower definition targets welfare benefits and anti-trafficking protection; critics warn it excludes many trans men, trans women and non-binary people. A Supreme Court-appointed advisory panel asked the government to withdraw the bill, calling removal of self-identification a setback against the 2014 ruling; presidential assent is pending. India is estimated to have around two million transgender people.
